'''Rodolfo "Rudy" Fernández Farrés''' ({{IPA|es|ˈruði feɾˈnandeθ}}; born 4 April 1985) is a Spanish former professional [[basketball]] player who spent the majority of his career for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He is a {{convert|6|ft|5|in|abbr=on}} tall [[Swingman#Basketball|swingman]]. He is a three-time [[All-EuroLeague Team]] selection and won the [[EuroLeague]] title in [[2014–15 Euroleague|2015]], [[2017–18 Euroleague|2018]] and [[2022–23 EuroLeague|2023]]. During his stint in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), he was an [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] member.

Fernández represented the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spanish national team]] internationally, and became the most capped player ever for Spain, with 266 matches.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/club/announcements/comunicado-oficial-rudy-fernandez-16-08-2024 | title=Real Madrid C.f. - Error }}</ref> He has won two [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA World Cup]] titles, in [[2006 FIBA World Championship|2006]] and [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019]], two [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympic]] silver medals in [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008]] and [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012]], as well as a bronze medal at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]]. He also won four [[EuroBasket]] titles in [[EuroBasket 2009|2009]], [[EuroBasket 2011|2011]], [[EuroBasket 2015|2015]] and [[EuroBasket 2022|2022]], a silver medal in [[EuroBasket 2007|2007]], and a bronze medal in [[EuroBasket 2013|2013]]. Fernández earned an [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-EuroBasket Team]] selection in 2009.

==Professional career==
===Joventut (2002–2008)===
[[File:Rudy Fernández.JPG|130px|thumb|left|With [[Joventut Badalona|DKV Joventut]] at the [[2008 ACB Playoffs]].]]
Rudy Fernández won the 2005 and 2007 [[Catalan basketball league|Catalan Tournaments]], the 2006 [[FIBA EuroCup|FIBA EuroChallenge]] championship, the 2008 [[Spanish Basketball King's Cup|Spanish King's Cup]] title, and the 2008 [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] championship, while playing with [[Joventut Badalona|DKV Joventut]] of the [[Liga ACB|Spanish ACB League]].

He also won numerous personal awards while playing with DKV Joventut, such as the 2004 [[Spanish Basketball King's Cup|Spanish King's Cup]] [[Most valuable player|MVP]], the 2006 [[FIBA EuroChallenge Final Four MVP]], the [[EuroLeague]] [[2006–07 Euroleague|2006–07 season]]'s [[EuroLeague Rising Star|Rising Star]] award, the 2008 [[Spanish Basketball King's Cup|Spanish King's Cup]] MVP, the 2008 [[EuroCup Basketball Finals MVP|EuroCup Finals MVP]], and the 2007 [[Catalan basketball league|Catalan Tournament]] Final MVP.

He was also named the 2006 [[FIBA Europe Young Men's Player of the Year Award|FIBA Europe Young Player of the Year]].<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/cid_pA6QsLQ,HlAYvAnY0Hd4U3.coid_w15-Ve3TGfgKnujAvEMrk3.articleMode_on.html Fernández wins European Young Player of the Year Award.]</ref> In July 2007, his contract with Joventut was extended through the year 2011, however his contract was bought out early in the year 2008 so that he could join the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]]. On his exit out of the club he paid tribute to his DKV coach, [[Aíto García Reneses]], "All I know of basketball is thanks to Aíto García Reneses", he said.<ref name="the jump"/>

===Portland Trail Blazers (2008–2011)===
[[File:Portland Trail Blazers crop.jpg|thumb|With the [[Portland Trail Blazers|Trail Blazers]] in December 2008.]]
On 28 June 2007 Fernández was taken 24th overall in the [[2007 NBA draft|NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]], who subsequently traded his draft rights along with [[James Jones (basketball, born 1980)|James Jones]] to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for cash. Rudy Fernández announced at a press conference on Friday 6 June 2008 that he would leave [[Joventut Badalona|DKV Joventut]] to join the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for the [[2008–09 NBA season]], and he signed a contract with the Blazers on 1 July.<ref name="oregonlive" /> "They [Portland] have shown a lot of interest in getting me and have assured me that I will be an important part in the team", he said.<ref name="the jump"/> Fernández joined the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] team on 22 September 2008.<ref>Jason Quick, [http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2008/09/rudys_rousing_arrival.html Rudy's rousing arrival], 22 September 2008</ref> He became the eighth Spaniard to play in the NBA.<ref name="the jump">{{cite web |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/p/langid/1/newsid/25503/arti.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121011180852/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/p/langid/1/newsid/25503/arti.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 October 2012 |title=Rudy makes jump to the NBA |date=6 June 2008 |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=28 June 2011}}</ref> For the [[2008–09 NBA season]] he joined several other fellow Spaniards in the league that included [[Pau Gasol|Pau]] and [[Marc Gasol]], [[José Calderón (basketball)|Jose Calderón]], and Trail Blazers teammate [[Sergio Rodríguez]]. He entered the NBA following his participation with the [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics|2008 Olympic basketball tournament]] in [[Beijing]], China.<ref name="oregonlive">{{cite news |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/blazers/2008/07/its_official_blazers_sign_rudy.html |title=It's official: Blazers sign Rudy |author=Sean Meahger |publisher=OregonLive.com |date=1 July 2008 |access-date=2008-07-01}}</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080818140949/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/fibaEven/olymMen/p/newsid/25503/arti.html ESP – Rudy makes jump to the NBA] FIBA.com, 6 June 2008</ref>

Fernández played in his first regular-season NBA game on 28 October 2008, coming off the bench to score 16 points in a 96–76 Portland loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=281028013 |title=Blazers-Lakers box score |access-date=26 January 2009 |date=28 October 2009 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>  On 12 November 2008 Rudy scored 25 points in 29 minutes against the [[Miami Heat]], including 8 of 8 from the free throw line adding to his already 92% FT shooting to set a new NBA career high.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20081101/PORPHX/gameinfo.html |title=Blazers-Suns box score |work=NBA.com}}</ref> On 18 January 2009 it was announced that Fernández had won the fan voting and was picked the fourth dunker to go to the [[NBA Slam Dunk Contest]] as part of the [[2009 NBA All-Star Game|2009 All-Star Weekend]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fernandez headed to All-Star weekend for dunk On 9 March 2009, against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], Fernández was taken off the court in a stretcher after Trevor Ariza hit him on the head on a fastbreak attempt. Fernández was alert and conscious when leaving the court with full movement of his extremities, however, he was taken to the hospital due to chest pain.<ref>{{cite web |title=Roy scores 27 in Blazers' 111–94 win over Lakers |work=NBA.com |access-date=10 March 2009 |date=10 March 2009 |first=Anne |last=Peterson |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20090309/LALPOR/recap.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161010060601/http://www.nba.com/games/20090309/LALPOR/recap.html |archive-date=10 October 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released from the hospital the next day with a bruised chest and a right [[hip pointer]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fernandez released; Odom suspended |date=10 March 2009 |first=Joe |last=Freeman |access-date=10 March 2009 |publisher=[[OregonLive.com]] |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/behindblazersbeat/2009/03/fernandez_released_odom_suspen.html}}</ref>

Fernández was selected to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] on 30 April 2009. He set NBA rookie records for number of three-point field goals made (159), hitting a three-point field goal in 33 consecutive games, and making a three-pointer in his first 20 career NBA games.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rudy Fernandez Named To NBA All-Rookie Second Team |first=Ben |last=Golliver |date=30 April 2009 |publisher=blazersedge.com |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2009/4/30/860325/rudy-fernandez-named-to-all-nba}}</ref>

On 16 October 2009 Blazers announced that they had exercised the third year of their option on Fernández's contract, keeping him with the team through the 2010–11 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail_blazers_exercise_options_2009_10_16.html |title=Trail Blazers Exercise Options On Oden, Fernandez, Batum, Bayless |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=16 October 2009 |access-date=2009-10-17}}</ref>

In December 2009, Fernández underwent [[Discectomy|microdiscectomy]] surgery for a [[herniated disc]] that was causing [[sciatica|leg pain]].<ref name="oregonlivesciatica">{{cite web |last=Meagher |first=Sean |title=Blazers G Rudy Fernandez to miss 4–6 weeks after microdiscectomy |url=http://blog.oregonlive.com/blazers/2009/12/rudy_fernandez_to_undergo_proc.html |work=OregonLive.com |date=9 December 2009 |access-date=24 November 2010}}</ref>

2010 |access-date=2011-09-16}}</ref> On 17 December 2010 he hit 9-of-15 shots and four 3-pointers for a career-high 26 points with six assists in a 107–102 win against [[Minnesota Timberwolves|Minnesota]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/32260010/ns/sports-player_news/ |title=Rudy Fernandez scores career-high 26 in win |work=[[msnbc]] |date=18 December 2010 Fernández struggled offensively for a good part of the year, but his improved play in other areas of the game has earned him praise from his peers. Blazers head coach [[Nate McMillan]], who isn't known to hand out compliments easily, singled out his defensive play in the second half of [[2011 NBA Playoffs#(3) Dallas Mavericks vs. (6) Portland Trail Blazers|Game 4 against the Mavericks]] as the key to the 84–82 win.<ref name="eurobasket11"/>

===Real Madrid (2011)===
On 21 September 2011 Fernández signed a one-year contract with the [[Liga ACB]] team [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], valid only while a new [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA collective bargaining agreement]] remained under negotiation.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 September 2011 |title=Real Madrid inks Rudy Fernandez |publisher=ESPN |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/story/_/id/6995918/dallas-mavericks-guard-rudy-fernandez-signs-real-madrid |access-date=6 December 2014}}</ref> Fernández signed for a reported salary of 2.7 million [[euros]] [[net income]] per season, the largest contract in Spanish league history, at that time. His deal also gave him the option to return to Real when his NBA contract ended.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 September 2011 |title=Rudy Fernández, blanco perfecto |language=es |work=Deportes.elpais.com |url=https://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2011/09/20/actualidad/1316503316_850215.html |access-date=6 December 2014}}</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2011–2012)===
During the 2011 NBA Draft Rudy Fernández was traded to the Mavericks in a three-team trade.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mavs trade picks for Rudy Fernandez |work=ESPN.com |date=24 June 2011 |access-date=3 September 2011 |url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=6698707}}</ref> However, he never played for the Mavericks, as he was traded with [[Corey Brewer]] to the [[Denver Nuggets]] on 13 December 2011. The Mavericks received a second-round draft pick and a traded player exception.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/fernandez_brewer_trade_12_13_2011.html |title=Nuggets acquire Brewer, Fernandez from Mavericks |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=13 December 2011 |access-date=2011-12-14}}</ref>

He played 31 games for Denver before suffering a season-ending back injury. In July 2012, Fernández announced he would not return to the NBA, opting for a 3-year deal with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hochman |first1=Benjamin |title=Rudy Fernandez, former Nuggets guard, will play in Spain |url=http://blogs.denverpost.com/nuggets/2012/07/05/rudy-fernandez-nuggets-guard-play-spain/6908/ |access-date=6 December 2014 |work=Denverpost.com |date=5 July 2012}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid (2012–2024)===
On 4 July 2012 Fernández returned to Real Madrid by signing a three-year deal<ref>{{cite news |title=REAL MADRID brings back Fernandez |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2012-13-signings/i/98404/7224/real-madrid-brings-back-fernandez |access-date=6 December 2014 |work=Euroleague.net |date=4 July 2012}}</ref> worth 9 million euros net income.<ref>[https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20120703/baloncesto/acb/rudy-fernandez-real-madrid-ficha_54320208223.html Mundodeportivo.com Rudy Fernández ficha por el Real Madrid {{in lang|es}}.]</ref> In May 2014, alongside his teammate [[Sergio Rodríguez]], he was named to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]] of the [[2013–14 Euroleague|EuroLeague]], the second consecutive in his career.<ref>{{cite web |title=2013-14 All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/136869 |work=Euroleague.net |access-date=9 May 2014}}</ref>

On 14 August 2014 he signed a three-year extension with Real Madrid, to stay in the club until 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid extends All-Euroleague swingman Fernandez through 2018 |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/140143/real-madrid-extends-all-euroleague-swingman-fernandez-through-2018 |access-date=27 June 2015 |work=euroleague.net |date=14 August 2014}}</ref> In May 2015, he was chosen to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague Second Team]] for his performance during the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xtj7vjfuokfw7g8 |access-date=8 May 2015 |work=euroleague.net}}</ref> Real Madrid won the [[2014–15 Euroleague|EuroLeague 2014–15 season]] championship, after defeating [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]], by a score of 78–59 in the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|final game]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid is Euroleague champion for record ninth time! |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=251&seasoncode=E2014#!report |access-date=18 July 2015 |work=euroleague.net |date=17 May 2015}}</ref> Real Madrid finished the season winning the [[2014–15 ACB season|Spanish League 2014–15 season]] championship, after a 3–0 series sweep in the ACB finals against [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]]. With that trophy, they finished the season having won the [[European Basketball Triple Crown|triple crown]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid make it 4 out of 4 |url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/06/24/en/football/real_madrid/1435176357.html |access-date=24 June 2015 |work=marca.com |date=24 June 2015 |language=es}}</ref>

In May 2018, Real Madrid won the [[2017–18 EuroLeague]] championship, after defeating [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe Doğuş]] in the [[2018 EuroLeague Final Four|final game]] with 85–80.<ref name="EuroLeague18Champ">{{cite news |title=Real Madrid is 2018 EuroLeague champion |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=260&seasoncode=E2017#!report |access-date=20 May 2018 |work=euroleague.net |date=20 May 2018}}</ref> Over 30 EuroLeague games, Fernández averaged 7.5 points, 2.6 assists and 2.4 rebounds per game. One month later, the club won the [[2017–18 ACB season|Spanish league]] after a 3–1 series win against [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]]. Fernández was named [[ACB Finals Most Valuable Player Award|MVP of the finals]].

On 2 July 2018 he signed a two-year extension with Real Madrid, to stay in the club until 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Champs, Fernandez pen new deal through 2020 |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8tuyfqwd3oimtegd |website=EuroLeague.net |date=2 July 2018 |access-date=2 July 2018}}</ref>

On 16 August 2024, Fernández retired from basketball.<ref>{{cite web |first=Javier |last=Gancedo |title=Rudy Fernandez says goodbye to basketball after Spanish elimination |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/rudy-fernandez-calls-time-on-a-glittering-career/ |website=EuroLeagueBasketball.net |date=16 August 2024 |access-date=17 August 2024}}</ref>

==National team career==
===Junior national team===
Fernández has been participating in international basketball competitions since he was sixteen years old. He played at the [[FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] and at the [[FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] with the Spain national junior teams.

[[File:Rudy Fernandez Eurobasket 2011.jpg|240px|thumb|left|Rudy at the [[EuroBasket 2011]].]]
===Senior national team===
As a member of the senior [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain national team]], Fernández competed at the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Summer Olympics]], averaging 5.1 points per game, in 10.6 minutes per game. The next year, he played at the [[EuroBasket 2005]], but his statistics were worse: 2.7 points per game, in 16.3 minutes, with a 31.6% FG%<ref>{{cite web |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/3769/tid/362/_/2005_EuroBasket/accumulated-statistics.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711000028/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/team/p/sid/3769/tid/362/_/2005_EuroBasket/accumulated-statistics.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 July 2011 |title=Spain accumulated statistics |publisher=Archive.Fiba.Com |date=25 September 2005 |access-date=2011-09-16}}</ref> His third appearance with Spain's senior national team was at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]], where he became an important player for the Spanish team, and contributed with 9.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.4 steals per game, to help his team win a gold medal.

He also played at the [[EuroBasket 2007]], where Spain won the tournament's silver medal. During this tournament, Rudy averaged 9.9 points in 20.3 minutes per game. At the [[Basketball at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]], Spain lost to [[United States men's national basketball team|Team USA]] in the gold medal match. Fernández scored 22 points in 18 minutes of play, with 5 three-point goals, and completed a dunk over [[Dwight Howard]]<ref name="interbasket">{{cite news |url=http://www.interbasket.net/news/453/2008/08/27/video-rudy-fernandez-dunk-on-dwight-howard |title=Video: Rudy Fernández dunk on Dwight Howard |publisher=Interbasket.net |date=27 August 2008}}</ref> that [[ESPN]] sportswriter [[Bill Simmons]] described as "hellacious".<ref>{{cite news |last=Simmons |first=Bill |title=Is it a classic if no one is watching? |date=11 September 2008 |publisher=ESPN The Magazine |url=https://www.espn.com/espnmag/story?section=magazine&id=3575385}}</ref> During the Olympics, Fernández had the following stats: 13.1 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 2.1 assists, in 22.3 minutes per game.

The [[EuroBasket 2009]] in Poland was his sixth consecutive appearance with the Spain national team. Spain won its inaugural gold medal in a European Championship, and Fernández averaged 13.2 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 2.1 steals per game, in 28.4 minutes, and was named to [[EuroBasket All-Tournament Team|the All-Tournament Team]].

In the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], Fernández averaged 15.6 points, 6.0 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.8 steals per game, but Spain only took sixth place in the tournament. Fernández then participated in [[EuroBasket 2011]],<ref name="eurobasket11">{{cite web |url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/p/langid/1/newsid/46647/arti.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110513020942/http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fc/news/lateNews/p/langid/1/newsid/46647/arti.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 May 2011 |title=ESP/USA – Rudy reflects on Blazers' season, confirms EuroBasket participation video |date=9 May 2011 |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=25 June 2011}}</ref> where Spain won the gold medal, and clinched a spot in the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]],<ref>[http://www.torontosun.com/2011/09/18/spain-repeats-as-eurobasket-champ Spain repeats as EuroBasket champ]</ref> where he won a silver medal with Spain. He also played at [[EuroBasket 2013]], where he won a bronze medal, at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], at [[EuroBasket 2015]], where he won a gold medal, at the [[Basketball at the 2016 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2016 Summer Olympics]], where he won a bronze medal, at the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], where he won a gold medal, at the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]], and at the [[EuroBasket 2022]], where he won a gold medal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 September 2022 |title=Rudy Fernández - Player Profile - FIBA.basketball |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/player/135508/Rodolfo-Fernandez |access-date=2022-09-19 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref>

At the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Paris 2024 Olympic Games]], he became the first male player to compete in six editions of the [[Basketball at the Summer Olympics|Olympic Games]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rudy's sixth sense: A unique olympic record |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/rudys-sixth-sense-a-unique-olympic-record |website=fiba.basketball |access-date=12 February 2026 |location=Lille, France |language=en-UK |date=23 July 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fernández married [[Helen Lindes]], his girlfriend of three years, on 4 July 2015. They live in Pozuelo de Alarcón, on the outskirts of Madrid. His older sister, [[Marta Fernández (basketball)|Marta Fernández]], played in the [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]] for the [[Los Angeles Sparks]] in 2007.
